overallFinding.summary: OKX has exact Poland-specific public evidence for operating its Europe exchange in Poland, including spot trading, staking, localized service and EUR cash rails, plus an OKX policy that explicitly lists Poland as a permitted country for core crypto-asset services. Polish KNF separately records a 2026 payment-services notification for OKX Europe Limited and an investment-firm notification for OKX Europe Markets Limited. Public PLN P2P buy/sell surfaces are live. Because account, product and regional eligibility remain conditional, the appropriate draft Poland posture is AVAILABLE_WITH_LIMITS for core regulated services rather than blanket availability.
overallFinding.recommendation: Treat core OKX Europe exchange/custody/transfer and spot services in Poland as a candidate AVAILABLE_WITH_LIMITS research posture. Treat PLN P2P and EUR SEPA rails as supported with limitations. Keep direct PLN bank rails not verified. Keep the investment-product layer separately available_with_limits/conditional under the separate investment-firm regime. Keep Poland referral/bonus and exact CBW referral binding under review.

methodologyNotes: No login, account creation, registration attempt, KYC submission, payment, deposit, withdrawal, trade, referral-code submission or financial transaction was performed.
Exact Poland product/launch evidence was kept distinct from generic EEA/MiCA or foreign-regulator context.
KNF payment-services and investment-firm notifications were treated as separate regulatory regimes/entities and were not collapsed into crypto/CASP authority.
PLN P2P public surfaces were not treated as proof of a direct PLN bank-deposit or bank-withdrawal rail.
A generic EEA investment-product statement was used only together with the Poland-specific KNF investment-firm notification and retained account-level limitations.
The CBW owner-confirmed global OKX affiliate URL/code was treated as commercial identity only, never as Poland referral/bonus eligibility evidence.
